In [[mathematics]], particularly [[functional analysis]], the '''Dunford–Schwartz theorem''', named after [[Nelson Dunford]] and [[Jacob T. Schwartz]], states that the averages of powers of certain norm-[[bounded operator]]s on [[Lp space|''L''<sup>1</sup>]] [[Limit of a sequence|converge]] in a suitable sense.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Dunford |first1=Nelson |last2=Schwartz |first2=J. T. |title=Convergence almost everywhere of operator averages |journal=Journal of Rational Mechanics and Analysis |volume=5 |year=1956 |pages=129–178 |mr=77090 }}.</ref>

==Statement ==
Let <math display="inline">T</math> be a linear operator from <math display="inline">L^1</math> to <math display="inline">L^1</math> with <math display="inline">\|T\|_1 \le 1</math> and <math display="inline">\|T\|_\infty \le 1</math>. Then

: <math>\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^kf</math>

exists almost everywhere for all <math display="inline">f\in L^1</math>.

The statement is no longer true when the boundedness condition is relaxed to even <math>\|T\|_\infty\le 1+\varepsilon</math>.<ref>{{Citation |last=Friedman |first=N. |title=On the Dunford–Schwartz theorem |journal=Zeitschrift für Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie und verwandte Gebiete |volume=5 |issue=3 |year=1966 |pages=226–231 |doi=10.1007/BF00533059 |mr=220900 |s2cid=122257150 |doi-access=free }}.</ref>
